questions.prompt: According to the Claude docs, what is by far the most important factor in tool performance?

options.explanation: Names help, but the docs name extremely detailed descriptions as the top factor.

options.text: The order of the tools in the list
options.explanation: The docs point to descriptions as the top factor, not list order.
Right. What it does, when to use it and when not, each parameter, and caveats.
The docs do not rank this. The description comes first.

questions.prompt: What does OpenAI suggest for the number of functions available at the start of a turn?

options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs call this a soft suggestion. The Gemini docs give a similar range: 10 to 20 active tools.

options.text: Exactly one, so the model never has to choose
options.explanation: OpenAI does not say this. It says keep the number small for higher accuracy.

options.text: As many as possible, so every request can be served
options.explanation: More tools add ambiguity and input tokens. The OpenAI docs suggest keeping the number small.

questions.prompt: What does strict mode do for tool inputs?

options.text: It makes tool inputs follow your JSON Schema instead of best effort.
options.explanation: Right. The Claude docs say strict mode guarantees inputs match the schema; the OpenAI docs say calls reliably adhere to it.

options.text: It makes the model always call one of the tools before it writes any text.
options.explanation: That is tool choice, a separate setting covered in chapter 4.

options.text: It checks that the tool's result is true.
options.explanation: Strict mode is about the input the model sends, not the result your tool returns.
